\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Hierarchy: Introduction}

\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Hierarchy: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Universal Simulation with a Space Bound]
\lean{Complexity.space_universal}
\label{Complexity.space_universal}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code, Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.pairEncode}
There exists a finite-state binary Turing machine $S$ such that for every binary word
$\alpha$ there is a positive integer $C$ with the following property: for every
$s,t\in\mathbb{N}$ and binary words $x,y$, if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ halts on
input $x$ after exactly $t$ steps with output $y$ and uses at most $s$ work-tape cells
by that time, then $S$ halts on input $\langle
\mathrm{bin}(s),\langle\alpha,x\rangle\rangle$ with output $y$ at some time and uses at
most $Cs$ work-tape cells by then. Here $\mathrm{bin}(s)$ is the little-endian binary
representation of $s$, and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the specified self-delimiting
pairing of binary words.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space hierarchy theorem]
\lean{Complexity.space_hierarchy}
\label{Complexity.space_hierarchy}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.SpaceConstructible}
Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be space-constructible functions. Suppose that for
every $A\in\mathbb{N}$ there is an $N$ such that $A f(n)\le g(n)$ for every $n\ge N$.
Then $\mathrm{SPACE}(f)$ is a proper subset of $\mathrm{SPACE}(g)$, where each class
consists of languages decidable by a finite binary Turing machine using at most a
constant multiple of the indicated space bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Strict inclusion of log space in polynomial space]
\lean{Complexity.LOGSPACE_ssubset_PSPACE}
\label{Complexity.LOGSPACE_ssubset_PSPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.PSPACE}
The class of languages decidable by finite Turing machines using space bounded by a
constant multiple of $\log_2(n)+1$ is a proper subset of the class of languages
decidable using space bounded by a constant multiple of $n^c+1$ for some natural number
$c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linear space differs from NP]
\lean{Complexity.SPACE_linear_ne_NP}
\label{Complexity.SPACE_linear_ne_NP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.SPACE}
The class of binary languages decidable by finite Turing machines using space bounded by
a constant multiple of the input length plus one is not equal to the class of languages
having polynomially bounded witnesses verifiable in polynomial time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Full-bank embedding of a configuration is trivial]
\lean{Complexity.f6_full_embed}
\label{Complexity.f6_full_embed}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitCfg_eq}
\difficulty{3}
Let $m\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $c$ be a configuration of an $m$-tape machine on a binary input.
Embedding $c$ into $m$ tapes along the identity map of tape indices, with an all-blank frame,
all frame heads at $0$ and empty prior output, gives back $c$ itself.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Run of a two-phase seamed machine]
\lean{Complexity.f6_seam}
\label{Complexity.f6_seam}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.seamCompTM, Turing.seamCompTM_step}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M_1,M_2$ be $k$-tape binary machines with control sets $S_1,S_2$ ($S_1$ with decidable
equality), let $e\in S_1$ and $n,q_2\in S_2$, and let $\Sigma$ be the seamed composite on
$S_1\sqcup S_2$ that runs $M_1$ and, from state $e$, takes one stationary silent dispatch step to
state $n$ of $M_2$. Suppose $M_1$ run from $c_0$ for $T_1$ steps reaches $c_1$, which is in state
$e$ while no earlier configuration is; and $M_2$ run from $c_1$ (control replaced by $n$) for
$T_2$ steps reaches $c_3$, which is in state $q_2$ while no earlier configuration is. Then $\Sigma$
started from $c_0$ (control injected on the left) is at time $T_1+1+T_2$ equal to $c_3$ with control
injected on the right, that configuration is in the right copy of $q_2$, and no earlier
configuration of $\Sigma$ is in that state.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Complexity.f6_hosted}
\label{Complexity.f6_hosted}

\lean{Complexity.f6_ruler_moves}
\label{Complexity.f6_ruler_moves}

$j\in\mathbb{N}$ let $W_j$ denote the tape contents $\beta$ together with $1^j$ written from cell

at $N+1$). (i) The skip machine on tape $r$, started in its running state with tapes $W_\ell$ and
all heads at $0$, reaches its done state after exactly $\ell+1$ steps, and not earlier, with the

with the head of $r$ at $\ell$ and everything else unchanged. (iii) The rewind machine on tape $r$,
started in its start state with tapes $W_N$ and the head of $r$ at $N$ (other heads at $0$),
reaches its done state after exactly $N+2$ steps, and not earlier, with all heads at $0$ and
everything else unchanged.
\end{theorem}

of $U_0$ on $x$ at radius $g(|x|)$ for $t+1$ rounds, starting from the initial configuration with

\uses{Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.SPACE.mono_const, Complexity.SpaceConstructible, Complexity.logSpace_eq, Complexity.mem_SPACE_iff, Complexity.spaceConstructible_iff, Complexity.sphEmitTM, Complexity.sph_emit_run, Complexity.sph_valid_machine, Complexity.sph_validated_machine, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.FinNDTM.acceptsWithin_iff, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.spaceUsed_le_of_halt, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.configBound, Turing.FinTM.decidesInSpace_of_alphabetReduction, Turing.FinTM.toFinNDTM, Turing.FinTM.toFinNDTM_haltsWithin_and_accepts_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg_eq, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_runWith, Turing.RecSym.digitEmb, Turing.RecSym.digitEmb_apply}
\difficulty{6}
Let $M$ be a finite binary machine with $k$ work tapes and state set $Q_M$, write
$\mathrm{cb}_M(n,s)=(|Q_M|+1)(n+2)\,3^{k(2s+1)}(2s+1)^{k}$ for its configuration count, and let $g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be
space-constructible. Then there is a language $L\in\mathrm{SPACE}(g)$ such that for all binary
words $x,w$: if $M$ has halted on $x$ with output $w$ by time $\mathrm{cb}_M(|x|,g(|x|))$ and visits
at most $g(|x|)$ cells by that time, then $x\in L$ exactly when $w\ne[1]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Linear space differs from NP via padding]
\lean{Complexity.sph_linear_ne_NP_of_padding}
\label{Complexity.sph_linear_ne_NP_of_padding}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode, Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.SpaceConstructible, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_id, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_polyUnary, Complexity.preimage_mem_NP, Complexity.spaceConstructible_linear, Complexity.spaceConstructible_poly, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Assume that for all space-constructible $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $A$ there
is $N$ with $A\,f(n)\le g(n)$ for all $n\ge N$, we have $\mathrm{SPACE}(f)\subsetneq\mathrm{SPACE}(g)$.
Assume moreover that for every binary language $L\in\mathrm{SPACE}(n^2+1)$ the padded language
$\{\langle x,1^{(|x|+1)^2}\rangle : x\in L\}$, with $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ the self-delimiting
pairing of binary words, belongs to $\mathrm{SPACE}(n+1)$. Then
$\mathrm{SPACE}(n+1)\ne\mathrm{NP}$.
\end{lemma}
